> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `eef9018534e603d6804fe065bd465548d1a4f989`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-activation-door-live.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/actions-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json (generated by the ledger's --write, read not reviewed) + packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts (NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS, NAMESPACE_REFUSED_LITERALS, readNamespacePositionSegment), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (getNamespaceOwners, the address-literal gate, refuseNamespaceObjectNameClashes), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (actionHandlerObjectKeys, standaloneActionOwnsRoute), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts outside the hunks (collectActionDeclarations, pickActionHolder, resolveRouteActionDeclaration, refuseDisabledPackageObject, loadActionSubjectRecord, the MCP run_action body), packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (readMergedItems, readServedObjects, readServedActions), packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (the createHonoApp catch-all), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts on main (the base arity read), docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md on main (D2, D3, D5, D6/Q3, "Covered and uncovered types", execution plan row G1)

Inputs read: card #31691 body and its six comments (triage 6727758204, ui carry-in 6727995849, E4 carry-in 6729429263, claim 6740163322, part (a) dev report 6744067280, B carry-in 6750690282); part (a)'s five records on PR #31959 for their lessons; PR #31979 body and file list; the net diff of `eef901853` against `main` (10 files); the check-runs on the head. The PR is a draft. At review time nothing has concluded `failure`. `success`: Check Changeset (both), Lint ESLint, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs. `in_progress`: Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Type Check workspace, consumer gates and debt ledger, Lint CI/release/engine gates, the two scoped lints (query-options erasure, slot lookup), Live E2E UI. The landing waits on those; this record judges the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New accept-set: `POST /actions/:ns/:object/:action[/:recordId]`, `/actions/:ns/global/:action`, and the same under `_env`.** The first segment is read once by `readNamespacePositionSegment('actions', ...)` in D5's order: the door's literals (the empty segment, `_activation`, `global`), then `_env`, then an installed namespace (`registry.getNamespaceOwners`), else bare. RIGHT against ADR-0150 D5 and its grammar table. The read sits after the anonymous baseline (first statement), the 405 and the engine resolution, so an anonymous caller gets 401 and learns no namespace. The namespace-to-package mapping is G2's (`getNamespaceOwners` handed to `resolveActionByName`), not a second one. RIGHT.
2. **Shareable namespaces (`base`, `system`, `sys`).** The addressed call filters the declarations to the namespace's owners and hands them to `pickActionHolder`, which refuses two package holders with `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`. `resolveAddressedRouteActionDeclaration` maps that to `refusal`, and the door answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with every candidate. It never picks. RIGHT against D2 (line 102 on main), and pinned (two co-owners of `crm`, 409 naming both, nothing run; ablation 5 red). `_env` keeps only rows with no package, so it has one holder by construction and a package-only name answers 404 naming the environment. RIGHT. `global` is a door literal and is read before any namespace, so it never resolves as one. RIGHT.
3. **Literal namespaces from part (a)'s R1.** Of the six refused literals, only `global` is a literal of this door. A boot-held package under `actions`, `connectors`, `hooks`, `oauth` or `trigger` is read as a namespace here and its qualified `/actions` address works. A boot-held package under `global` is never reached by a qualified `/actions` path, because the literal wins; it stays reachable by the bare name while it is the one holder and by MCP `run_action` with `namespace`. It shadows no literal route. RIGHT, and the same cost part (a) accepted.
4. **Object-versus-namespace ambiguity.** The read re-reads a bare path whose first segment equals an installed namespace. Child K (merged, `refuseNamespaceObjectNameClashes`, at every install, boot included, no downgrade) keeps a namespace from equalling an object name in either direction, so no declared object's bare path changes. What does change is the accident the bare door has always served: an object-less action answers under ANY first segment (`standaloneActionOwnsRoute` admits an object-less owner for every routed object, and an unknown object passes `refuseDisabledPackageObject`). So on base `/actions/crm/log_call` ran a one-holder object-less `log_call` whoever held it, and `/actions/crm/lead/convert` ran an object-less action named `lead` if one existed. Both are now the namespace's alone. This is D5 step 2 as published ("a first segment that names an installed namespace is the namespace"), so it is RIGHT in kind, but the changeset's "each such path answered 404" is not true of these (④ 1).
5. **The four-segment mount** `POST {base}/actions/:ns/:object/:action/:recordId`, declared domain-decides-every-verb. It cannot shadow a three-segment mount (different arity) nor `/actions//:action`. A four-segment path whose first segment is no address is declined (`handled: false`) and the mount answers the dispatcher's 404 `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. A deeper `_activation` path is declined inside the activation door, after its two gates, so a caller the gates refuse still gets 403 and the gate is not narrower than its route. RIGHT on the mounted host. WRONG as described for the catch-all host (④ 1).
6. **Gate order on the addressed path.** After the strip, the path runs the bare door's own sequence unchanged: disabled-package object refusal, declaration, 409 refusal, degraded 503, no-declaration 404, the ADR-0066 D4 permission gate, the activation consult, the handler-owner refusal, the param contract, the caller-scoped record load. The qualifier narrows which declaration is read and never skips a gate. RIGHT. The 404 that names the namespace and the 409 that names the holders both precede the D4 gate, as the bare door's own "no declaration" 404 does (④ 7).
7. **The carry-in (`addressedActionHits`).** Bound to the object first, then the holder's object-less one, inside ONE holder set. It cannot pick across packages, because the candidates are filtered to the namespace's owners (or to package-less rows) before the fallback. It runs nothing the caller could not run bare: the bare door already admits an object-less declaration on any routed object, with or without a record id, and the same D4, activation and owner gates judge the resolved declaration. The record is loaded in the caller's own scope (`callData` with the caller's execution context), as bare. RIGHT on REST. The MCP side reaches the same declaration but not the same subject (④ 3).
8. **`ActionAddressQualifier` and `resolveAddressedRouteActionDeclaration`** are new exports of runtime, and `resolveActionByName`'s qualifier parameter widens to the union. Additive. RIGHT.
9. **Two existing pins edited, not one.** The dogfood pin (acceptance[1], the transport's byte-identical 404 becomes `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`) is named in the PR body. The runtime pin in `actions-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts` ("a four-segment /actions path no route serves answers the transport's 404") was moved to five segments; the PR body does not name it as an edited pin. Both follow from the mount and are RIGHT; name the second one.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/runtime` with a BREAKING banner, a FROM/TO line and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. This matches AGENTS.md step 3: the kind is `none`, and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner. RIGHT. Part (a) was `minor` because it narrowed what an author can write (the namespace value); this part does not.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. RIGHT: no key, value or type an author writes is added or refused here. The literal-namespace refusal shipped in part (a).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. RIGHT in kind: the addressed paths are new surface, and one existing answer changes.
- The BREAKING text is incomplete and partly wrong about what the change replaces (④ 1). The level does not move; the text does.
- Only `runtime` publishes a change. The dogfood and script paths publish nothing. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question, the four-segment answer: keep the mount and `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`.** The status stays 404. `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` is what a `createHonoApp` host already answers for a path no domain serves, so the two host shapes converge on one answer. The fallback-seam alternative does not reach zero change either: the domain's anonymous baseline is its first statement, so an anonymous caller would still move from the transport's 404 to 401 unless the seam read the namespace table ahead of authentication, and that would tell an anonymous caller which namespaces are installed. A third copy of the transport's unmatched body is worse than either. The condition is ④ 1: say truthfully what each host answered before.
- **Escalation to the epic seat.** The card's Narrowing line lists three narrowings, and this PR's is none of them. The card's acceptance says a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer before landing. On the mounted host the change is a 404 code for a path that was never a route, which the epic seat can reasonably take as its own call. On a catch-all host it is a served call becoming 404 (④ 1). The epic seat should see that fact stated before it accepts, and decide whether it needs the maintainer.
- **Open question, names:** `ActionAddressQualifier`, `resolveAddressedRouteActionDeclaration`, `resolveEnvironmentActionDeclaration`, `addressedActionHits` read well and match G2's vocabulary. No new error code is minted, as D5 requires. Accepted.
- **Open question, SDK:** `server-only` on the three rows is right while the SDK names no namespace; child U or a client card carries it.
- **Follow-up card owed** for ④ 4 if it is not pinned here (the collector is G2/E2 code outside this diff).
- **Carry-ins not owed by this part:** the ui pair-read pin and the E4 activation 409 landed with part (a); B's agent/skill qualified-read pin (6750690282) is owed by part (c) or a `/meta` follow-up, not by `/actions`.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against D5 on main: the ledger's bare grammar ends at `/actions/:object/:action/:recordId`, and no ledger row, SDK builder or ADR line ever declared a fourth bare segment. Declining it makes the published grammar real; it takes no declared capability away. The narrowing is sound. The findings are about how far it reaches and how it is described.

1. **SHOULD-FIX: on a catch-all host the declined path was SERVED on base, and the PR says it was a 404.** `createHonoApp` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`, `app.all(prefix/*)`) hands every path to `dispatch()`. On main, `handleActionsRequest` reads `parts[0..2]` and has no upper bound on the segment count, so `POST /api/v1/actions/task/close/rec_1/extra` ran `close` on `task` for `rec_1` and ignored the rest, and `POST /actions/_activation/OBJ/ACT/extra` answered the door's shape 400 behind its gates. On the head both are declined and answer 404 `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. The changeset says "Before, the transport answered its unmatched 404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND for it" and "It is still no route"; the comment in `actions.ts` says each transport answers it "as the path nothing serves it answered before that mount existed"; the comment in `dispatcher-plugin.ts` says "as on a catch-all host". None of these is true of that host. The same decline also covers five and more segments there. Fix, prose plus two comments: state both hosts in the BREAKING block and the PR body (mounted host: transport 404 becomes dispatcher 404; catch-all host: a call that ran with its trailing segments ignored becomes 404, and the deeper `_activation` 400 becomes 404), correct the two code comments, and correct "each such path answered 404" for the object-less accident in ① 4. Add one pin on a catch-all dispatch for the decline. First-party count stays 0. This is the fact the escalation in ③ rests on.
2. **SHOULD-FIX: the addressed remainder has no arity bound, so the door accepts shapes D5 does not publish.** After the strip only an empty remainder and `_activation` are refused.
   - One segment: `POST /actions/crm/log_call` (two segments, through the existing `/:object/:action` mount) is read as crm's object-less `log_call`. D5's table, the ledger rows, the changeset and this door's own 404 sentence ("An addressed action path is /actions/:ns/:object/:action[/:recordId] or /actions/:ns/global/:action") name no such shape, and no test drives it.
   - More than three: on a catch-all host `POST /actions/crm/task/close/r1/extra` is served with the tail ignored, while the bare path is now declined past three and the mounted host answers the transport's 404 for it (the edited every-verb pin). The two hosts disagree on a path this PR introduces.
   Fix: after the strip, require two or three segments; answer the shape 404 this door already has for one, and decline more than three as the bare arm does. Pin both, each with a CONTROL. If the one-segment spelling is wanted, it needs a ledger row, the grammar table and a pin instead.
3. **SHOULD-FIX: the carry-in is "the same declaration" on both doors, but not the same call.** REST keeps the routed object: `/actions/crm/lead/log_call/r1` loads `lead` record `r1` in the caller's scope and dispatches under `lead`. MCP takes the object from the resolved row: `run_action(log_call, { namespace: crm, objectName: lead, recordId: r1 })` falls back to the object-less row, so `objectName` becomes `global`, `loadActionSubjectRecord` skips the load, and the handler runs with no record and `params.objectName` `global`. The two pins compare `packageId` only, so they cannot see it. The changeset sentence "The MCP run_action call with a namespace reads the same rule" is true of resolution only. Either carry the caller's `objectName` through the MCP fallback so both doors hand the handler the same subject, or declare the difference and pin it (assert `obj` and the record on both doors). The MCP arm is G2's code; if it is not changed here, say so in the changeset and file the card.
4. **SHOULD-FIX (pin here, or a card): an object-bound action that a second package binds to another package's object is not reachable by its address.** `collectActionDeclarations` drops a standalone declaration whose `objectName:name` key an object-embedded one already holds, whatever package ships it ("object-embedded declaration wins"; `seen` is not keyed by package). Failure case: `lead` (crm) embeds `convert`, and hr ships a standalone `convert` bound to `lead`. `POST /actions/hr/lead/convert` answers 404 "not found on object 'lead' in namespace 'hr'"; if hr also holds an object-less `convert`, the fallback serves that one instead. ADR-0150 "Covered and uncovered types" says of exactly this pair that "a package-qualified address reaches the intended one". The collector is outside this diff and is read, not reviewed, but this PR is the first REST consumer and its object-bound pin has no embedded competitor. A declared capability not delivered is an implementation gap: pin the pair in this PR (each address reaches its own), or file the card against the collector and name the gap in the changeset. It is not to be narrowed at this door.
5. **NIT: the `_activation` ledger row's note is now stale**, in a file this PR edits: "The dispatcher mounts three `/actions` patterns" and "A 4-segment path resolves to NOTHING and 404s at the router". There are four mounts, and the four-segment path reaches the door and is declined behind its gates.
6. **NIT: `readMergedListing` is a second copy of `readMergedItems`** (`domains/mcp.ts`), the same body. One reader, exported from one place, keeps the two doors on one listing shape.
7. **NIT, tried and held: what an under-privileged caller learns.** Anonymous: nothing, 401 first on every shape and verb. Signed in without the action's `requiredPermissions`: the addressed 404 naming the namespace and the 409 naming the holders both precede the D4 gate. The bare door already answers "no declaration" 404 before its 403, so an action name's existence is no new fact. The new facts are that a namespace is installed and, for a co-owned shareable namespace, the holders' package ids. The gate cannot be asked before a pick, because `requiredPermissions` belongs to each declaration. MCP's qualified call answers the same way, through the same resolver. This differs from part (a)'s should-fix, where a type-level gate existed and was skipped. If the seat wants it tighter, refuse 403 when the caller fails the gate of every candidate; that is a follow-up, not a defect of this head.
8. Tried and held: `/actions/NS/_activation/...` and `/actions/_env/_activation/...` answer the shape 404 and write nothing; a namespace cannot spell `_env`, `_activation` or the empty segment; a second-segment `global` under an address is the object-less key and never a namespace; the three-segment addressed shapes rebuild byte-identically through the `:recordId` mount; a refusal, a degraded metadata plane and a 404 stay three different answers on the addressed path (409, 503, 404).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mjoky7`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmPF1skfu2kx89BEXZi`

**VERDICT: PASS** (four should-fixes; a delta review of their fixes is owed before landing, and ③'s escalation goes to the epic seat)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `791c2723912b05b494b298e159b4feba0e4ca36f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts, .changeset/31691-actions-addressed-call.md + packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (the catch-all's unhandled answer), every other path unchanged since eef90185

Delta review of record 6751465170 (head eef90185, PASS, four should-fixes). One commit, 791c2723, no merge, no rebase.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Should-fix 1 (hosts) is closed, with one correction to the record accepted.** On a catch-all host, `dispatch()` answers `{handled:false}` for the declined path and `createHonoApp`'s `toResponse` writes its own 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, not `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. The BREAKING block now says both hosts answer 404 with their own codes. On a mounted host, the transport's `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` becomes the dispatcher's `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. On a catch-all host, a call that ran with its tail ignored, or the deeper `_activation` 400, becomes 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. The object-less accident under a namespace-named first segment is stated as a second narrowing. The first-party count is 0 for both. Both code comments are corrected. Pinned at the `dispatch()` seam, because runtime cannot import the hono adapter: bare and addressed paths past three segments are declined and run nothing, with a CONTROL. Right.
2. **Should-fix 2 (arity) is closed.** After the strip, the addressed remainder must be 2 or 3 segments. One segment answers the door's shape 404, and more than three is declined like the bare arm (the `!addressQualifier` exemption is gone). Both are pinned with CONTROLs. Right.
3. **Should-fix 3 (MCP subject) is closed.** When a qualified `run_action` names an object and resolution falls back to the holder's object-less row, the caller's `objectName` and its object are kept. The gates, the record load and the dispatch then see REST's subject. Pinned on both doors by `obj` and the record, not by `packageId` alone. Right.
4. **Should-fix 4 is declared.** The `collectActionDeclarations` gap (a standalone action of one package bound to another package's object is shadowed by an embedded one) is named in the changeset and the body. The seat files the card. The collector is unchanged here, because keying it by package would also narrow the bare door. Right.
5. **Nits are closed.** The `_activation` ledger note is current. `readMergedItems` is one export in `action-execution.ts`, and the `mcp.ts` copy is gone. The second edited pin (actions-every-verb) is named in the body.
